HelloFresh Group is building the next generation of consumer experiences across its portfolio—from discovery and personalization to shopping and subscription management. The Consumer UX team is at the heart of this work, designing end-to-end experiences that are simple, delightful, and grounded in real customer needs.
This role requires a Senior UX Designer who brings an entrepreneurial mindset, a high craft bar, and the agency to push for the right solution. The scope involves working on complex consumer problems with real business impact, collaborating across product, engineering, and brand in an environment that values curiosity, speed, and quality in equal measure.
This role holds accountability for end-to-end design projects and helps establish processes that drive success across the team and organization. It does not include people management responsibilities.

Consumer Experience Design: Lead design from concept to execution, maintaining accountability for the full experience across consumer touchpoints, and holding a high bar for quality at every stage of that arc.
AI-Native Workflow: Use AI as an active part of the workflow—generating and synthesizing user insights, accelerating discovery, building rapid prototypes, and closing the gap between design and code to move faster and think sharper.
Raise the Craft Bar: Bring a keen eye for detail across every layer—layout, motion, typography, micro-interaction—and hold that standard within the cross-functional unit. Use animation and motion as strategic tools to make experiences feel alive and intentional.
Opportunity Identification: Identify and explore product opportunities through market research and user analysis, translating insights into informed design decisions.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with product leads, engineers, and other stakeholders to align design strategies with business goals and technical requirements. Make confident decisions with cross-functional partners and advocate clearly and persistently for the right design outcome.

Experience: Minimum of 6 years of experience in product design, with a proven track record of delivering high-quality consumer products end-to-end.
AI-Native Design Skills: Active use of AI tools across the design workflow—for strategy, insight synthesis, discovery, rapid prototyping, and design-to-code development. Fluency with tools like Figma AI, Claude, and similar is expected.
Craft Excellence: Exceptional visual and interaction design skills with a high personal bar. Deep focus on details—hierarchy, motion, micro-interaction, animation—and the ability to articulate design quality standards effectively. Experience using motion to elevate product quality is a strong plus.
High Agency: Proactivity to push for the right technical solution rather than the convenient one, bringing conviction to design decisions and collaborating effectively with cross-functional partners.
Communication: Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate design concepts and decisions effectively upward and across business functions.

Global collaboration at scale: Collaborate with experienced engineers and product partners across HelloTech’s international teams, in a culture of active knowledge sharing.
Technology with real-world impact: Build and operate modern systems at global scale, supporting 6+ millions of customers and complex supply chain operations.
Technical/Product/Design leadership: Drive best practices and influence architecture/design, quality, and ways of working in an autonomous, product-led setup.
End-to-end development/delivery: Drive decisions from problem definition to production, improving systems and enabling long-term scalability.
Access to workspace at Warsaw Centre Point: The hub offers modern facilities including showers, breakout zones, outdoor space, cycle parking, and refreshments (coffee, soft drinks, and fruit).

We're transforming the grocery industry
At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community.

We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.
Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.
Instacart is a Flex First team
There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Every year, people across the world spend nearly one trillion dollars on groceries. It’s an industry that’s been around for centuries. Food itself, however, has been a constant in people’s lives since the beginning of time. Yes, sustenance is essential, but it’s also much more than that.

Food can be a part of a daily ritual or a special moment that resonates with people on a meaningful and emotional level. It can be a much-needed break in a long day, a taste that brings back memories, a creative experiment, a shared meal with loved ones, or even comfort during a hard time.

Whether it’s a special occasion or an everyday occurrence, it should always be easy for people to get the ingredients they need.
The Instacart Design Team is dedicated to making grocery shopping effortless for everyone and finding solutions to large-scale opportunities that will forever change the way people feed themselves and their loved ones. We’re a four sided marketplace and design for the needs of Consumer, Shoppers, Retailers, and Advertisers.
Within the Instacart Design org, we have exciting roles that will drive meaningful business impact through thoughtful strategy, experimentation, and high-quality execution.

We design the end-to-end journeys that help customers discover, understand, and feel the undeniable value of Instacart, putting empathy for both prospective and existing members at the center of every decision. Our team blends product thinking, brand-forward storytelling, and behavioral insight to create cohesive, high-performing growth experiences.

We pride ourselves on a culture of experimentation, accountability, and craft, continuously evolving how we design for conversion, retention, and long-term customer value.
We’re hiring for a Staff Experience Designer to join the Core Experience team and lead work across multiple touchpoints along our end to end online grocery experience in app.

You’ll obsess user, cultural and industry shifts in food and shopping spaces and inspire new features that come with strong value propositions that can be uniquely owned by the Intacart brand experience and online grocery ecosystem.

This role will need to work very closely with teams across the end to end shopping experience as well as new modalities that help deliver experiences through AI and agentic based conversational interfaces.

This is a high-impact, highly collaborative role partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Marketing, Brand, Data Science, and Research to drive measurable business outcomes while strengthening customer trust, affinity for the brand and long-term loyalty.

Daily Rhythms and Samples of Work
Drive and lead experiences across consumer-facing products to create highly personalized journeys that meet households where they are — their routines, their needs, their goals — and build new layers of value into the core grocery experience.
Lead end-to-end experience design briefs across all surfaces and modalities, including agentic interfaces, that deepen how customers discover, shop, and build lasting habits with Instacart.
Craft narratives, naming, and value propositions for experiences and features, creating artifacts (strategy docs, flows, storyboards, internal decks) that help teams socialize strategies and ideas.
Define and own experience frameworks that map key journeys (first 3 orders, building repeat patterns, subscription adoption, household management) and clearly articulate the beats, rhythms, and jobs to be done at each step.
Shape content, hierarchy, and information architecture across surfaces: define how information is structured, named, and prioritized so users have clear comprehension at every step while the business and partners get the right visibility where it matters.
Codify experiential principles, functional and emotional, to guide what users should understand, decide, and feel across flows, then translate those principles into patterns, content hierarchies, and interaction rules that scale across teams.
Use AI-assisted prototyping and concept development as a core part of your practice, providing strong art direction, references, and experiential intent to generate flows and concepts that align with Instacart's design system, brand positioning, and evolving interaction patterns.
Design for visual clarity, pacing, and density, establishing patterns, grids, and rules that govern how modules, carousels, and key placements work (above vs. below the fold) to balance user needs, business objectives, and partner value.
Work with Research, and sometimes lead or plan it yourself, to uncover insights about how customers shop, build routines, and evolve over their lifecycle with Instacart, then translate those insights into concrete journey maps, flows, and experiential principles.
Raise the bar for experience-led thinking across the pods, mentoring partners on how to think in journeys and emotions rather than just screens, and advocating for cohesive, principle-driven experiences that feel uniquely Instacart.

15+ years of experience designing consumer-facing digital products and experiences across web and mobile, with a portfolio that highlights complex, multi-step journeys and end-to-end flows including marketing channels like social, crm, and campaigns.
Strong track record of projects that demonstrate a fluency and depth in at least two design languages: content design, UX/product design, visual design, design strategy, design research —and demonstrable fluency collaborating across the others.
Driven by continuity, consistency, cohesion, comprehension and brand differentiation with an exceptional eye towards design system detail.
Proven ability to partner with product and business leaders as you direct multiple design disciplines through clear briefs, concept iteration, testing, executive reviews and feature launches.
An overwhelming fascination with human behaviors, pop, food, social and shopping culture, communication, visualization, design systems, language, content hierarchy, and the evolving models of producing world class design products for our future conditions.

We are a certified B Corp, plastic-neutral, and on a mission to transform the CPG industry for good.

Grove is rebuilding its store. We are repositioning the entire company on Human Health — the idea that the products in your home shape the health of the people living in it. That position changes what we sell, how we talk about it, and what shopping at Grove should feel like. Our current site was built for a different Grove. It needs to be rebuilt.
We're hiring a Principal UX Designer to lead the design of that rebuild. This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Product Management & UX, who sets the overall vision for the customer experience. Your job is to turn that vision into a design direction concrete enough for Product and Engineering to build against — across the core flows, across the teams doing the work — and to see it through to launch.
This is the rare moment where a designer gets a blank page on a real business. Grove is a public company with millions of customers, a working commerce engine, and a leadership team that has decided to change direction. You will not spend a year building consensus for change. The change is already the mandate. Your job is to define what it looks like and get it live.
We're looking for someone who can hold the direction in one hand and a Figma file in the other. Someone who has done the rebuild before and wants to do it again with more room to swing.

Vision and strategy for the Core-Site Experience . In partnership with Sr. Director of Product, you will define, you will define what Grove's store should be and make that vision concrete enough that Product, Engineering, and leadership can build against it. You'll set the design principles, defend them in the room, and translate the Human Health positioning into an experience customers can feel on the first screen.
Design direction for the Core-Site rebuild. You'll translate the Human Health positioning into a design approach the teams can execute against, and set the design principles that hold the rebuild together. You'll make the calls on direction independently, and bring the cross-system trade-offs to your manager rather than deciding them alone.
The core flows, end to end. Homepage through category, search, product detail, cart, and checkout — you define how they hold together and how each one gets built. That includes the design system patterns that make the consistency real in code, designed for other people to implement, not just for you to hand off.
AI prototyping in the design practice. Today, strategic conversations happen against slides and get decided too late. You'll use AI prototyping in your own work every week, and partner with Engineering and the other UX Designers on the shared components and patterns that let the team put a real prototype on the table in days. When it works, we argue about a real experience early, while the argument is still cheap.
Walk The Store. You'll take part in the recurring series where the CEO and leadership team walk the live customer experience together, bring the design point of view into that room, and turn what surfaces there into prioritized work on the rebuild.
Craft across the design team. You'll mentor the designers around you, define what good looks like in practice, and raise the bar on craft. Grove should be a place where strong designers want to work, and you're a reason why.

You've done the rebuild. You've taken a real commerce experience apart and put it back together. You're comfortable when the answer is "start over," and you know how to sequence a rebuild so the business keeps running while you do it.
You hold the direction and go make it. You can carry a multi-quarter initiative and a two-week sprint in your head at the same time. You put pen to paper. You sit with Product and Engineering, cut scope, solve the hard state, and see it through to launch.
You have real e-commerce depth. You've designed at scale for consumers who are shopping, comparing, and deciding. You know how merchandising, search, and subscription mechanics shape an experience, and you design with the commercial reality in view. You understand the systems underneath well enough to know what your design choices cost to build.
You prototype with AI. You use it in your own work every week. You know what today's tools can and can't do, and you bring the rest of the design team along with you.
You can hold your own with senior leadership. You can present work to executives, advise on trade-offs and sequencing, take hard feedback without losing the thread, and change minds by putting better work on the screen.
You raise the people around you. You mentor generously, critique honestly, and make other designers better without needing the org chart to say you can.
Craft is non-negotiable. Interaction design, information architecture, visual design, and systems thinking — you're strong across all four, and fast in Figma.
